'''David Earl Wear Jr.''' (born September 21, 1990) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]] and the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. He played briefly with the [[Sacramento Kings]] in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) in 2015.

In high school, Wear won a silver medal for the United States national team at the [[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]]. He was named an [[All-American]] as a senior in 2009. He played in college for one season at North Carolina before transferring to UCLA. After going [[List of National Basketball Association undrafted players|undrafted]] in the [[2014 NBA draft]], he played most of 2014–15 in the NBA Development League (now known as the [[NBA G League]]), but also had a brief stint in the NBA with Sacramento. He then played two seasons in Spain with [[Baloncesto Fuenlabrada]] before joining Osaka.

==High school career==
Wear attended [[Mater Dei High School (Santa Ana, California)|Mater Dei High School]] in [[Santa Ana, California]] where he was a two-time [[California Interscholastic Federation]] State champion in 2007 and 2008. As a junior, he averaged 18.9 points and 10.0 rebounds per game. As a senior, he averaged 16.4 points and 7.5 rebounds per game.<ref name=bio>{{cite news |title=#12 David Wear |url=http://www.uclabruins.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30500&ATCLID=207913791 |work=uclabruins.com |accessdate=September 5, 2014}}</ref> Wear was selected as the 2009 county boys' basketball player of the year, a 2009 fourth-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]], a repeat first team all-county member, first team All-Division I-AA member, first team all-league member, second team all-state in 2009, and an all-state sophomore in 2007.<ref>{{cite news |title=David Wear - Mater Dei basketball - biography |url=http://www.ocvarsity.com/sports/david-13936-wear-mater.html |work=OCVarsity.com |date=August 4, 2008 |accessdate=September 5, 2014 |archive-date=September 24, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924054849/http://www.ocvarsity.com/sports/david-13936-wear-mater.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |first=Michael |last=O'Shea |title=High School Boys Basketball Team |url=http://parade.condenast.com/104308/michaeloshea/parade-all-america-high-school-boys-basketball-team/ |work=Parade.com |date=April 5, 2009 |accessdate=September 5, 2014}}</ref>

Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Wear was listed as the No. 16 power forward and the No. 59 player in the nation in 2009.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-David-Wear-55282;_ylt=AsqLvNdEbALy6q4xa.Jmr1hGPZB4 David Wear Recruiting Profile]</ref>

==College career==
Wear and his twin brother, [[Travis Wear|Travis]], played for the defending national champion [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]] in their freshman year.<ref name=foster_030422014>{{cite news |last=Foster |first=Chris |title=UCLA's twin Wear brothers near the end of their identical act |date=March 2, 2014 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |url=http://articles.latimes.com/2014/mar/02/sports/la-sp-ucla-wear-twins-20140302 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140910195230/http://articles.latimes.com/2014/mar/02/sports/la-sp-ucla-wear-twins-20140302 |archive-date=September 10, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Wear contributed 2.9 points and 1.7 rebounds a game while averaging over 10 minutes per game.<ref name=markazi/> The Tar Heels missed the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) tournament]], which upset their fans. Brother Travis said playing for North Carolina "wasn't what I thought it would be."<ref name=foster_030422014/> The twin brothers transferred after the season in May 2010 to UCLA.  They [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] the following season due to NCAA transfer rules.<ref name=markazi>{{cite news |last1=Markazi |first1=Arash |last2=Leung |first2=Diamond |title=Wear twins transferring to UCLA |date=May 25, 2010 |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/los-angeles/news/story?id=5219398 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100528224532/http://sports.espn.go.com/los-angeles/news/story?id=5219398 |archive-date=May 28, 2010 |url-status=live }}</ref>

UCLA won the [[Pac-12 Conference]] championship in [[2012–13 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2012–13]]. However, UCLA coach [[Ben Howland]] was fired after the season, prompting Wear and his brother to consider transferring. After meeting with incoming coach [[Steve Alford]], the brothers were convinced they fit as starters in the new coach's system.<ref name=foster_030422014/> On January 26, 2014, Wear scored a career-high 18 points against California, eclipsing his previous high of 17 in 2011, also against Cal.<ref>{{cite news |title=Wear's career-high leads UCLA past Cal 76-64 |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/wear-39-career-high-leads-031842799--ncaab.html |work=Yahoo.com |date=January 26, 2014 |accessdate=September 5, 2014 |archive-date=September 5, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140905192033/http://sports.yahoo.com/news/wear-39-career-high-leads-031842799--ncaab.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> At the team's annual banquet after the [[2013–14 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2013–14 season]], Wear was awarded the Irv Pohlmeyer Memorial Trophy, for being the team's top defensive player. He graduated following the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=UCLA Looks Forward to Thursday Evening's NBA Draft|date=June 24, 2014|work=uclabruins.com|url=http://www.uclabruins.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30500&ATCLID=209529910|accessdate=June 27, 2014}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===D-League and NBA (2014–2016)===
After going [[List of National Basketball Association undrafted players|undrafted]] in the [[2014 NBA draft]], Wear joined the [[Chicago Bulls]] for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=BULLS ANNOUNCE 2014 NBA SUMMER LEAGUE ROSTER|date=July 8, 2014|work=NBA.com|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-announce-2014-nba-summer-league-roster|accessdate=September 5, 2014}}</ref> On September 25, 2014, he signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-announce-training-camp-roster Kings Announce Training Camp Roster]</ref> However, he was later waived by the Kings on October 19, 2014.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/kings/kings-waive-bhullar-burton-wear Kings Waive Bhullar, Burton, Wear]</ref> On November 2, 2014, he was acquired by the [[Stockton Kings|Reno Bighorns]] as an affiliate player.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/reno/bighorns_finalize_training_cam_2014_11_02.html BIGHORNS FINALIZE TRAINING CAMP ROSTER AFTER D-LEAGUE DRAFT] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141106210413/http://www.nba.com/dleague/reno/bighorns_finalize_training_cam_2014_11_02.html |date=November 6, 2014 }}</ref> Wear's shooting ability allowed him to thrive in Coach [[David Arseneault Jr.]]'s [[run and gun (basketball)|run-and-gun]] system,<ref>{{cite news |last=Carpenter |first=Les |title=140 points a game – but are the Reno Bighorns a basketball experiment too far? |date=February 20, 2015 |newspaper=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2015/feb/20/140-points-a-game-but-are-the-reno-bighorns-a-basketball-experiment-too-far |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150220123715/http://www.theguardian.com/sport/2015/feb/20/140-points-a-game-but-are-the-reno-bighorns-a-basketball-experiment-too-far |archivedate=February 20, 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref> and he was invited to participate in the Three-Point Contest during the 2015 [[NBA Development League All-Star Game|D-League All-Star Weekend]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Schlosser |first=Keith |title=David Wear Discusses Playing In "The System" In Reno And Finding Early Success |date=February 18, 2015 |work=SBNation.com |url=http://www.ridiculousupside.com/2015/2/18/8058893/david-wear-discusses-playing-in-the-system-in-reno-and-finding-early-success |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150325100931/http://www.ridiculousupside.com/2015/2/18/8058893/david-wear-discusses-playing-in-the-system-in-reno-and-finding-early-success |archivedate=March 25, 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On March 23, 2015, Wear signed a 10-day contract with the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-david-wear|title=Kings Sign David Wear to a 10-Day Contract|work=NBA.com|date=March 23, 2015|accessdate=March 23, 2015}}</ref> He was not retained by the Kings following the expiration of his 10-day contract on April 2. In July 2015, Wear joined the [[Detroit Pistons]] for the Orlando Summer League and the Sacramento Kings for the Las Vegas Summer League.<ref name=sportando_08102015/>

===Overseas (2016–present)===
On August 10, 2015, Wear signed with [[Baloncesto Fuenlabrada]] of Spain for the 2015–16 season.<ref name=sportando_08102015>{{cite news|title=Fuenlabrada announces David Wear|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/172244/fuenlabrada-announces-david-wear.html|accessdate=August 10, 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=August 10, 2015}}</ref> On August 1, 2016, he re-signed with Baloncesto Fuenlabrada  for the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Fuenlabrada re-signs David Wear|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/208274/fuenlabrada-re-signs-david-wear.html|accessdate=August 5, 2016|work=Sportando.com|date=August 1, 2016}}</ref>

In 2017–18, Wear moved to Japan to play with [[Osaka Evessa]] in the [[B.League]]<ref>{{cite news|title=Osaka Evessa signs David Wear and Greg Smith|date=August 8, 2017|website=Sportando.com|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/243757/osaka-evessa-signs-david-wear-and-greg-smith.html|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170809091523/http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/243757/osaka-evessa-signs-david-wear-and-greg-smith.html|archivedate=August 9, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> and played with the [[Sydney Kings]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] in 2018–19.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/42189-sydney-kings-add-import-forward-david-wear|title=Sydney Kings Add Import Forward David Wear|work=NBL.com.au|date=May 26, 2018|accessdate=May 26, 2018|archive-date=May 27, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180527023329/http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/42189-sydney-kings-add-import-forward-david-wear|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Uluc|first=Olgun|title=NBL Free Agency Tracker — Fox Sports Australia|date=June 7, 2019|website=FoxSports.com.au|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nbl/nbl-free-agency-tracker-fox-sports-australia/news-story/230992e503d6236989733d514dbf3143|accessdate=November 10, 2019}}</ref>

==National team career==
In July 2008, Wear won a silver medal playing for the USA Basketball Men's U18 National Team at the FIBA Americas U18 Championship in Formosa, Argentina.<ref name="bio" />

==Personal==
Wear is the son of David Sr. and Gloria Wear. His father played college basketball at Fresno State and Cal State Fullerton and professionally overseas.<ref name="bio" /> His twin brother, [[Travis Wear|Travis]], also became a pro basketball player.

Wear's wife Christina played basketball professionally overseas.<ref>{{cite news|last=Sondheimer|first=Eric|title=Trinity League basketball media day provides insights into season ahead|date=October 29, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/highschool/story/2019-10-29/la-sp-trinity-media-day|accessdate=November 10, 2019}}</ref>
